rationale: The assistant initially took 'nn h98' as a model ('For a Panasonic NN-H98 not heating') rather than asking whether H98 was a display code, which was the sensible first clarification; the customer corrected this unprompted. Once the code and full model were known, it correctly read H98 as a high-voltage inverter/magnetron output fault, kept appropriate uncertainty ('most likely the inverter board or the magnetron'), and escalated to an engineer with consistent safety warnings against opening the case. No invented facts or unjustified parts, though it did not mention Panasonic service agents or the repair-vs-replace cost question.
